_README: #5072 (epic #5067): the panel rubric — a FIXED standard the training plan is graded against, one seat per school of the training charter's concession_ledger (the seat keys must equal the ledger's keys; tests/test_panel_rubric_5072.py holds it). Each criterion is graded by CODE (a named check in lambdas/training/panel_rubric.py CHECKS, ADR-105: deterministic computation before any model verdict) or by the JUDGE (lambdas/training/panel_judge.py, route charter.judge / charter.judge_gate) when code cannot check it. The concession each seat makes is READ from the charter at grade time, never copied here. The target (overall letter, every-seat floor) is the charter's panel_target. Hand-owned; a change is a new version with a change_log line.

change_log.what: the eight seats, 40 criteria (32 by code, 8 by the judge), the letter scale

overall_rule: the overall score is the mean of the eight seat scores, mapped through `letters`; a seat score is the mean of its criteria; the target is met only when the overall letter reaches the charter's panel_target.overall AND every seat reaches panel_target.every_seat_at_least

calibration.rule: the judge is uncalibrated until the owner has graded this many plans by hand and the judge's seat scores sit within 1 point of his on each; every grade carries its calibration state

criteria.text: every lifting movement carries the double progression's verdict (step, hold, floor raise or re-entry) with its reason
working sets carry a rep range wide enough for double progression to run
the accessory layer rotates on the charter cadence instead of freezing
weekly hard sets for the priority muscles sit between MEV and MAV
each priority muscle gets at least one movement loaded in its lengthened (stretch) position, and the exercise choices are the high-stimulus, low-fatigue options for this trainee
single-leg lower-body work appears at least twice a week
loaded carries appear at least once a week
corrective / posture work (face pulls, Pallof press, rear delts, rotator cuff) appears at least twice a week
pulling volume at least matches pressing volume
the plan keeps some athletic carryover (multi-planar, unilateral, trunk stability) and does not read as machines-only bodybuilding
weekly sets per priority muscle sit inside MEV-MAV
the charter's MEV-floor muscles appear in every lifting session
legs are held at or above their maintenance floor (MEV)
no deload is scheduled or applied without the owner's recorded word
volume is distributed so per-session junk volume is avoided and fatigue is managed without a scheduled deload
the progression and stall rules are coded, not improvised
every lifting day carries a tracked anchor lift
the anchor-strength tripwire is evaluated, so muscle loss is caught early
effort is prescribed by RPE on the lifting movements
numbers in the plan's reasons are stated with their basis (his own data vs population defaults); nothing claims more certainty than the evidence carries
conditioning is split hard/easy with the charter's number of hard sessions
every cardio block carries a dose: minutes, a level/speed/incline and an RPE or talk test
weekly fatigue signals are wired into a deload recommendation
the daily step floor is carried by the plan
hard conditioning is placed to limit interference with the heavy lower day and recovery
carries or kettlebell work every week
the week covers hinge, squat, push, pull and carry
no session runs past the charter's lifting-minute cap
the same few big lifts repeat across the week
the plan is simple enough to execute for months — the goal stays the goal, no novelty for its own sake
the charter's number of lifting days
every lifting session sits inside the charter's lifting-minute band
delts are trained the charter's number of times a week
the step floor and target are carried every day
the plan reads like a time-bound transformation: aesthetic priorities (delts, lats, upper chest, arms) get the emphasis and nothing in the week wastes the deadline
effort is prescribed by RPE
no automatic deload; a deload only on the owner's word
conditioning is prescribed by RPE or the talk test
the recovery, protein, strength and weight-stall tripwires are evaluated every week
the week's total dose (lifting days, conditioning, steps) is sensible for fast loss, with warm-ups on the heavy lifts and the hardest work spread out
